analysis.title: GS - Sharkey - Extremes - 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: GS net sold $4.2bn of tech on Friday, the largest single-day tech sell skew in 3 weeks, and finished the week as net sellers, fully reversing a +$5bn mid-week buy skew.
At the peak of the current unwind GS net sold $21bn of TMT, versus $23bn in the July AI sell-off.
Early-week tech re-risking faded after disappointing mega-cap prints: INTC on PC weakness, AMZN on weak FCF and higher buyside AWS bogeys, search weakness, and MSFT beating but closing lower.

NDX vs S&P Equal Weight had its worst month of underperformance since 2002. SOX closed below its 200dma for the first time since June 2025 and is 27.1% below its local high after 355 consecutive sessions above it.
Software outperformed Semis by 27% in the month, the 2nd biggest monthly outperformance since 2015 and the second-best month in 10 years.
AI vs 'AI at Risk' (GSPUARTI) had its second-worst month since the launch of ChatGPT, while S&P ex-AI posted +7.64%, its best month since the launch of ChatGPT.
Global TMT-focused L/S funds are down 11.9% MTD (-3.1% on Friday, -2.2 SD) and +5.7% YTD. The HF VIP vs VIP Short basket had its 3rd worst month in 15 years.

Global Fundamental L/S managers lost 85bps Friday (-1.3 SD), driven by beta and Info Tech, and are down 3.3% MTD but up 9.3% YTD. Global Systematic L/S lost 70bps Friday, are down 3.7% MTD (first negative month of the year) and up 16% YTD.

Mag7 was net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, but exposure is near YTD highs and at the top of its 5-year range after going from under-owned in June. GS expects the group to keep acting as a source of funds, limiting dip-buying demand. Retail is flagged as a wildcard.

Global equities were net bought for the first time in a month (+0.3 SD 1-year) even as de-grossing continued for a 3rd straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.8 to 1. Macro products (index and ETF) made up 73% of net buying, the largest in 3 months.

Hedge fund gross leverage is 314.1% (85th percentile 1-year, 97th percentile 5-year). Net leverage is 73.6% (10th percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage is 49.3% (3rd percentile 1-year) and beta-adjusted net leverage is 64.8%, a 1-year low.
GS says P&L protection takes priority over P&L generation, which limits offense in the near term.
Brazil had its largest net selling among EM regions in 5 years, led by long selling exceeding short selling.

Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in recent decades outside post-recession recoveries, but ending the pattern of acceleration. The size of the beat versus estimates is smaller than in Q1 and Q2.
Defensives are bid: BRK/B, KO, PM, ABBV and AAPL (acting defensive) all hit all-time highs within the last 2 weeks.

Midterm baskets: a Democratic sweep favors ACA beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) through revived enhanced subsidies. AI Power (GSENEPOW) is preferred over ex-Power AI hardware (GSTMTAIH). 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated from corporate tax changes, with the risk a higher rate beyond 2029 (GSPUTAXP).

sector_views.rationale: Software beat Semis by 27% in the month and SOX broke its 200dma. The note describes the move and does not issue a rating.
BRK/B, KO, PM, ABBV and AAPL hit all-time highs in the last 2 weeks and the note says the bid for defensives remains strong.
In a Democratic sweep scenario, reviving enhanced subsidies helps hospitals, providers and insurers.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y (estimate, season in progress), matching Q2, but it would end the pattern of acceleration of recent quarters.
Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS has exceeded estimates by a smaller magnitude than in Q1 and Q2.

INTC reported negative EPS reaction on PC weakness. AMZN reported weak FCF and higher buyside AWS bogeys, with search weakness noted. MSFT beat and closed in the red. No figures are given in the note.

macro_indicators.interpretation: On track to match Q2 as the strongest quarter in decades outside post-recession recoveries, but growth is no longer accelerating.

trade_ideas.rationale: Reviving the enhanced subsidies helps hospitals, providers and insurers.

trade_ideas.description: Long AI Power basket (GSENEPOW) over ex-Power AI hardware basket (GSTMTAIH)
trade_ideas.rationale: Increasing power supply is portrayed as the fix for electricity inflation, while policymaker convergence on datacenter cost bearing could weaken datacenter project economics and weigh on ex-Power hardware.

risk_factors: Continued unwinding of AI-related length and Mag7 selling as a source of funds.
Hedge fund P&L pain and a focus on capital protection limiting dip-buying.
Slowing earnings momentum, with smaller beats versus estimates in Q3.
Weaker datacenter project economics if policymakers push datacenter operators to bear power costs.
